newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 47,250 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 46.302 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in the U.K. received 14,000 tonnes, in Denmark 13,000, in Belgium 10,000, in France 10,000 and in Germany 250 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.346 million tonnes. This compares with the 53,400 tonnes awarded on January 10, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.439 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to be 45.296 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 40,000 and 70,000 tonnes versus 44,500 last week when the restitution was 45.902 Ecus.
